input.title: RESOLVE_CALLER_IDENTITY makes Switchboard verify the bearer and populate ctx.user without switching the policy from OPEN to ADMIN_ONLY

input.description: AUTH_ENABLED both selects ADMIN_ONLY and verifies tokens; this flag separates the two. It defaults to AUTH_ENABLED, resolves an identity but enforces nothing, and an invalid token is still a 401.

metadata.reason: Extracted from apps/switchboard/Auth.md at v6.2.2-dev.74 — Basic Configuration › Environment Variables Method: RESOLVE_CALLER_IDENTITY matrix
Adds a fourth knob to the host authorization flow: identity resolution decoupled from the OPEN/ADMIN_ONLY policy selection that AUTH_ENABLED drives

input.content:
`AUTH_ENABLED=true` does two things: it selects the authorization policy (`ADMIN_ONLY` instead of `OPEN`) **and** it makes the middleware verify the bearer so `ctx.user` is populated. `RESOLVE_CALLER_IDENTITY` separates the second from the first:

| | `AUTH_ENABLED` unset | `AUTH_ENABLED=true` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RESOLVE_CALLER_IDENTITY` unset | no user, `OPEN` | user resolved, `ADMIN_ONLY` |
| `RESOLVE_CALLER_IDENTITY=true` | **user resolved, `OPEN`** | user resolved, `ADMIN_ONLY` |

It defaults to whatever `AUTH_ENABLED` is, so a deployment that never sets it behaves exactly as before. The bold cell is the combination `AUTH_ENABLED` alone cannot express, and the one a **custom subgraph needs when it does its own authorization**: its resolvers learn who is calling without every non-admin being locked out of the switchboard.

It *resolves* an identity and enforces nothing — a request with no token is still admitted, with no user. Verification is otherwise identical to `AUTH_ENABLED=true`, Renown credential check included, so an invalid token is still a 401. (Upstream, this landed in 6.2.2-dev.73 and dev.74 fixed a regression it introduced: with the flag on, a tokenless WebSocket subscription was refused until dev.74 admitted it when only resolving identity.)

_Source: apps/switchboard/Auth.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.74)._
